issues.title: Unsupported functional orthogonality

failure_location.quote: If \cref{eqn:beta-Tucker} present the orthogonal Tucker tensor, then $\{T_{0:m_\ell-1}(x_\ell)V^{(\ell)}\}$ appear to be the set of $r_\ell^0$ orthogonal polynomials.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: which forms a sequence of orthogonal polynomials on $[-1,1]$ with respect to the weight $w(x) = 1/\sqrt{1-x^2}$.

issues.failure_explanation: The prose proof establishes the functional Tucker factorization, but not its final orthogonality clause. For example, with m_ell=r_ell=2 and V=(1/sqrt(2))[[1,1],[1,-1]], the two functions are (T_0+T_1)/sqrt(2) and (T_0-T_1)/sqrt(2). Since the stated Chebyshev weight gives squared norms pi and pi/2 to T_0 and T_1, respectively, their weighted inner product is pi/4 rather than zero. Moreover, T_{0:m_ell-1}V has r_ell entries, not the asserted r_ell^0 entries unless additional factors or equalities are imposed.
issues.overall_effect: The functional Tucker representation and its use in later error estimates remain valid, but the proposition does not establish orthogonal functional factors. No later formal result requires that extra property.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the false orthogonality clause by a weighted Gram normalization. For the reduced factors B^(ell)=V^(ell)G^(ell), use the Chebyshev Gram matrix D_ell=diag(pi,pi/2,...,pi/2), set M_ell=(B^(ell))^T D_ell B^(ell), and replace B^(ell) by B^(ell)M_ell^(-1/2), absorbing the corresponding invertible changes of basis into the core. This gives exactly r_ell^0 weighted-orthonormal polynomial factors while preserving the represented function, degrees, and Tucker ranks.
issues.why_classification: The proof makes a genuine invalid inference from Euclidean orthogonality of coefficient vectors to weighted functional orthogonality, so this is not a typo. Nevertheless, weighted QR or Gram normalization is a short, standard, mode-local Tucker reparametrization that also fixes the r_ell versus r_ell^0 mismatch and requires no new substantive result or downstream repair.

new_version_repair_locator.quote: that is, each entry of $v^{(\ell)}$ is a linear combination of Chebyshev polynomials.

issues.title: Mode-independent DCT terminal index
issues.failure_explanation: An m_ell by m_ell inverse DCT matrix for the old basis T_0 through T_{m_ell-1} must end with T_{m_ell-1}. If, for example, m is read as the maximum mode degree and m_ell=2<m, the displayed two-row mode matrix uses T_0 and T_{m-1}, rather than T_0 and T_1, and need not be invertible or implement the required mode transform. No isotropy assumption excludes this admissible case.
issues.overall_effect: For anisotropic polynomial degrees, the displayed matrix and every algorithm invoking it can compute the wrong coefficient tensor. The isotropic specialization m_1=m_2=m_3 is unaffected.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: In the old indexing convention, replace every T_{m-1} in the terminal row of W^(ell) by T_{m_ell-1}. No other part of the DCT construction or its uses needs to change.
issues.why_classification: The asserted m_ell-by-m_ell matrix and the explicitly stated basis T_0 through T_{m_ell-1} uniquely force this correction directly from the old source. It is a mode subscript transcription error, not a defect in the DCT reasoning.

issues.title: RHOSVD complexity claim

failure_location.quote: the memory and computational cost are both $\mathcal{O}(mR)$.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: \cref{alg:cheb_tuck_alg_cp_2}: $C_6 nR + C_7 mR + C_9 m R\log m + C_{10} mR \min\{m,R\} + C_{11} R |\log \varepsilon|^3$.

issues.failure_explanation: The prose claims that the CP-aware RHOSVD method has both storage and total computational cost O(mR). The old complexity proposition actually establishes additional spline, DCT, side-matrix SVD, and Tucker-core reconstruction costs, including mR log m and mR min{m,R}. Thus O(mR) can describe storage of the CP side factors in a simplified accounting, but it is not a uniform bound for the method's arithmetic cost. This materially overstates the algorithm's performance even though its advantage over the full-tensor method may remain.
issues.overall_effect: The remark gives a materially misleading linear-cost summary and an overstated basis for saying the RHOSVD variant is always preferred. The separately stated formal complexity proposition remains the correct diagnostic result and is not invalidated by the remark.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Rewrite the remark to distinguish the O(mR) storage of the CP coefficient side factors from total arithmetic work. State the established work bound O(nR+mR+mR log m+mR min{m,R}+R|log epsilon|^3), up to constants, and qualify the claim of preference by comparing this bound with the full-tensor alternative rather than saying the method is always preferred solely because of O(mR) work.
issues.why_classification: The existing complexity proposition supplies a contained repair without any new proof architecture, and the same RHOSVD algorithm and its data-sparse advantage survive. However, correcting the remark withdraws a substantive linear-time guarantee and its unconditional performance conclusion, so the issue exceeds a minor wording correction while retaining a recognizably comparable complexity claim.

new_version_repair_locator.quote: \cref{alg:cheb_tuck_alg_cp}: $C_5 nR + C_6 mR + C_7 m R\log m + C_{8} mR \min\{m,R\} + C_{9} R |\log \varepsilon|^3$.

issues.title: Signed CP-weight error bound

diagnostic_evidence.quote: where $\| \boldsymbol{\xi} \|_1 = \sum_{k=1}^{R} |\xi_k|$ is the $\ell_1$ norm of the normalization constants.

issues.failure_explanation: The lemma claims an absolute error is bounded by a sum of nonnegative interpolation-error factors multiplied by signed xi_k. For R=1, xi_1<0, and a nonzero interpolation error, that displayed right-hand side is negative while the left-hand side is nonnegative. The triangle inequality used in the proof requires |xi_k|. The lemma's subsequent definition of the l_1 norm already uses sum |xi_k| and therefore confirms the required correction.
issues.overall_effect: The lemma's first bound and its proof are invalid for the stated signed-weight convention. Consequently, the following unlabelled corollary and final unlabelled error theorem are not established by the written proof, although their norm-based conclusions are recovered by the same local correction.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Retain signed weights xi_k in the CP format, but replace xi_k by |xi_k| in the lemma's first bound and at every corresponding use of the triangle inequality in its proof. The resulting sum is bounded by ||xi||_1, so the stated norm-based corollary and final error theorem then follow unchanged.
issues.why_classification: The missing absolute values invalidate an actual triangle-inequality step, so the defect is substantive rather than typographical under the stated standard. The repair is nevertheless uniquely indicated by the existing definition of ||xi||_1, is entirely local and routine, and restores the lemma and both listed dependents with no loss of domain or guarantee.

issues.title: Full-tensor spline complexity

failure_location.quote: Similarly, the cost of trivariate cubic spline interpolation which is required in \cref{alg:cheb_tuck_alg} is $\mathcal{O}(m^3(m+n))$.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: \Require Given a tensor ${\bf F}\in \mathbb{R}^{n_1 \times n_2 \times n_3}$

issues.failure_explanation: The proof transfers the one-dimensional O(m+n) spline estimate to three dimensions by multiplying it by m^3. For n_1=n_2=n_3=n, however, constructing a spline that interpolates an arbitrary n^3-entry input requires processing the full three-dimensional data. Thus, for fixed or moderate m in the paper's intended m much smaller than n regime, the claimed O(m^3(m+n)) work understates the n-dependence. The corrected construction cost is O(n^3+m^3).
issues.overall_effect: The proposition substantially understates the time complexity of the full-tensor algebraic algorithm and consequently distorts its comparison with the CP-aware alternatives; the algorithm's mathematical output is not otherwise invalidated.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the trivariate spline-construction term by O(n^3+m^3) in the isotropic case, incorporate that term into the full complexity bound for the full-tensor algorithm, and revise comparisons with the CP-aware methods accordingly. More generally, the bound must account for processing all n_1 n_2 n_3 input entries and evaluating the requested interpolation grid.
issues.why_classification: For arbitrary full n-by-n-by-n input, merely processing the data imposes an Omega(n^3) lower bound. Thus, in the intended regime m much smaller than n, the old fixed-m linear dependence on n cannot survive; correcting it to cubic dependence is a major loss of the formal result's central complexity guarantee. Retaining the old rate would require a materially different input contract or proof and algorithm architecture, so no complete route avoids either major loss or global reconstruction.

new_version_repair_locator.quote: Similarly, the cost of trivariate cubic spline interpolation which is required in \cref{alg:cheb_tuck_alg} is $\mathcal{O}(m^3+n^3)$.

issues.title: Newton collocation-cell definition
issues.failure_explanation: In the isotropic case alone, the old definitions give t_0=-1-h and t_1=-1. Thus the first claimed basis cell lies outside [-1,1], whereas cells 2 through n provide only the n-1 physical cells that partition the interval. The equality between the domain integral and the displayed unrestricted cell integral therefore already fails for indices containing 1. Before the later isotropic simplification, the factor h^{-3} is also incompatible with the separately defined h_1,h_2,h_3.
issues.overall_effect: The displayed n by n by n projection-collocation tensor is not consistently defined by a partition of the stated domain; its first slabs and, in the anisotropic presentation, its volume normalization are wrong. Later application prose relies on the intended corrected tensor construction but no later old formal result proves a conclusion from the malformed indexing.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Adopt a consistent n_ell-cell convention: set h_ell=2/n_ell, define boundary points t_j^(ell)=-1+(j-1)h_ell for j=1,...,n_ell+1, integrate the i_ell-th basis function over [t_{i_ell}^(ell),t_{i_ell+1}^(ell)), and use the prefactor 1/(h_1 h_2 h_3). Update the isotropic shorthand consistently.
issues.why_classification: This is not a uniquely forced one-symbol typo because the old source mixes a grid-point convention with a cell convention and also needs a coordinated anisotropic normalization correction. It is nevertheless a standard, short local reindexing that restores a partition of the same domain and the intended projection-collocation tensor without changing the method, rates, or any dependent formal conclusion.
